summary: Smithers Airport (YYD) is a regional airport serving the town of Smithers and the surrounding Bulkley Valley in northern British Columbia, Canada. Nestled near the Babine Mountains and Hudson Bay Mountain, it functions as an important aviation gateway for remote communities in the region and a key stop for general aviation traffic crossing northwestern BC. The airport features a single asphalt runway and supports scheduled regional flights as well as bush plane and charter operations common to northern Canada.
faqs:
Q: Which airlines operate scheduled flights from Smithers Airport?
A: Air Canada Express (operated by Jazz Aviation) and Central Mountain Air historically have provided scheduled passenger service to Vancouver and other northern BC destinations. Service schedules can change, so checking current carrier listings is recommended.

Q: How far is the airport from downtown Smithers?
A: Smithers Airport is located only about 5 km (3 miles) north of the town center, typically a 5-10 minute drive.

Q: Does Smithers Airport have customs and immigration facilities?
A: The airport has limited CBSA (Canada Border Services Agency) services, primarily available by appointment for general aviation flights arriving from international origins. Scheduled flights from domestic Canadian destinations do not require customs clearance.

Q: Is there overnight parking available at the airport?
A: Yes, the airport offers free parking for both short-term and long-term stays in its public lot adjacent to the terminal building.
transport_tips: Rental cars are available at the airport from local agencies and are the most convenient option for exploring the Bulkley Valley and surrounding wilderness areas. Taxi services operate to and from Smithers town center, though advance booking is advisable as availability can be limited outside scheduled flight times. The short 5 km drive into town is straightforward via Highway 16 (Yellowhead Highway).
